hook: Supernova shocks in dense circumstellar shells can make fast soft X-ray flashes with blackbody-like spectra
summary: A model of supernova shocks breaking out of dense gas shells predicts X-ray flashes of 10^43 to 10^45 erg/s lasting under about 10^4 seconds. It matches the light curves and temperatures of three known events, including XRF 060218. It is a theoretical fit to three events, so the shell properties it infers depend on the model's assumptions.
title: Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
